title: What other shows deserve long-delayed cast albums?? #broadway #musica...
transcript: What is the deal with this rock opera from eight years ago by the songwriter of Hedwig and the Angry Inch suddenly getting an album all these years later? And could this happen for other shows? This Ain't no disco is a musical that played off Broadway at the Atlantic in 2018. It was written by Stephen Trask, who co-wrote Hedwig and the Angry, alongside Peter Yanowitz, who was actually the drummer for Hedwig on Broadway, and the two of them wrote this score and co wrote the book with Rick Elice. It followed a bunch of characters in the late 70s, sort of in the final days of Studio 54. Andy Warhol was a side character, but in particular it focused on Sammy, a young black singer, and Chad, a young gay dancer who worked at Studio 54. From what I remember the musical was not very well received, and I get it, I saw it,it was kind of a hot mess. There were too many subplots, too much going on, where I think they were trying to have a central story, but also be this panoramic snapshot of a time and place. And I think in the latter is more where the quality of the materials suffered. I preferred it when I was focusing on the central friendship, but I still kinda vibed with the gritty, passionate energy of it, and I liked most of the music, including on this relisten. The album actually only contains about half of the music that was in the show. Because the show was mostly sung through. It's also not really a cast album. It's a world premiere recording with songs from the musical. Only a handful of the original cast members are on it. Instead, it has featured artists like John Cameron Mitchell and Lena Hall. But what does this mean? Are they planning to bring the show back? Not necessarily. Trask and Yanowitz were on the Be Our guest podcast, and they indicated that this was more of a passion project they put together to have some tangible record of all the hard work they put in on this show. They mentioned in passing that some company in Australia was thinking of putting on the show, but otherwise this was not meant to gear up for some first class production return. Unfortunately, now that we know this kind of thing can happen, I'm going to become absolutely insufferable. Where is our oratorio for living things album? Dave Malloy’s Moby Dick? The Lucky Ones by the Bengsons? The Secret Life of Bees? Mamdani please, we need these cast albums.
